rubric_items.reason: All 12 known REQs and assumed REQ-13 are traced: S-1 has REQ-1 to REQ-5, S-2 has REQ-6, REQ-7 and REQ-2, S-3 has REQ-8, S-4 has REQ-13 and S-5 has REQ-9 to REQ-12.
Most stories have one outcome. S-5 bundles four separate non-regression constraints (paging, search, sort, privacy), and privacy is a different concern from list mechanics.

Every criterion is Given/When/Then. S-1 AC3 has no exact expected format (U-1). S-5 AC2/AC3 compare against 'before this change' with no stated baseline, so they can only be checked by regression comparison.
Every value comes from the intent: 'Next appointment', Asia/Kolkata, 20 per page, 'None'. No invented limits.
Readable and uses consistent glossary terms. Minor: S-3 AC1 says 'click the value' without saying which part (date/time or doctor name) is the link.

findings.text: Q-05 cites req.md#L127 as evidence. That line is the U-1 date-time format unknown, not the missing glossary terms Cancelled, Completed, patient list and front-desk staff.

cites.quote: The display format of the start date and time is not given.

findings.suggested_fix: Cite req.md#L139-L148 (U-5..U-8) or req.md#L196-L199 (glossary found:false entries) for Q-05.

findings.text: S-5 bundles four separate outcomes (page size, search, sort, no medical history) in one story. The privacy constraint has a different source and risk than the list-mechanics checks.

cites.quote: title: Keep the patient list's paging, search, sort and privacy unchanged

findings.suggested_fix: Consider splitting REQ-12 (no medical history in list) into its own story.

findings.text: S-5 AC2 and AC3 check against 'before this change' but give no baseline search or sort behaviour, so they can only be verified by a before/after regression run.

cites.quote: then the same patients are returned as before this change.
